researchMethod: Phase 6 operational layer - filings fetched/extracted programmatically (research.js), analysis performed directly by Claude Code reading the extracted material, not by an automated LLM API call. Every factual claim below cites a specific source in the sources[] list.

quantContext.note: From this project's own scoring pipeline (companies.json + screener.js, Phases 1-5/7), included for reference only - not itself a research source.

whyCheapBearCase.answer: CTSH trades at a moderate P/E (12.52) and low P/B (1.82) [source: 1] despite a genuinely improving FY2025 (revenue +7.0%, operating margin +140bps - see next question) [source: 4], and the stock is down -21.73% over 6 months [source: 1]. Two filing-confirmed, concrete reasons help explain the discount rather than pure quant inference. First, the 10-Q itself discloses that 'during the quarter ended June 30, 2026, the Company's common share price and market capitalization declined, reaching a recent low, before partially recovering in July 2026,' which triggered management to perform a formal qualitative goodwill impairment assessment (concluding no impairment, but the fact that a real, dated stock-price decline was material enough to require this review is itself informative) [source: 3]. Second, Cognizant discloses an ongoing Title VII employment discrimination class action (a 'bench-terminations class' certified by the court, with a jury trial already held in 2023 on the first phase) that remains unresolved as of the FY2025 10-K [source: 5]. A cached SeekingAlpha headline, 'Cognizant: Cognizant Of AI Fears, But Also Of The Opportunity' (2026-08-07), also names a live market narrative - fear that generative AI could disrupt Cognizant's core IT-services labor-arbitrage model - as a real, current bear-case theme, even though the 10-K itself frames AI primarily as an opportunity ('As an AI builder...') [source: 4, 8].

revenueEpsTrend.answer: Improving on a full-year basis, with a slight moderation visible in the most recent XBRL quarter. FY2025 revenue increased 7.0% (6.4% constant currency) to $21,108 million, aided 260bps by the Belcan acquisition [source: 4, 6]. GAAP operating margin rose 140bps to 16.1% and Adjusted Operating Margin rose 50bps to 15.8% [source: 4]. GAAP diluted EPS grew only 1.1% (to $4.56) because a one-time, non-cash $390 million income tax expense from the repeal of R&E cost capitalization under the OBBBA reduced FY2025 GAAP diluted EPS by $0.80; Adjusted diluted EPS, which excludes that charge, grew 11.2% [source: 4, 6]. The most recent XBRL data point available in this packet is Q1 2026 (ended March 31, 2026): revenue $5,413 million vs. $5,115 million a year earlier (+5.8%), diluted EPS $1.39 vs. $1.34 (+3.7%), while net income was essentially flat ($662 million vs. $663 million) and operating income dipped slightly ($843 million vs. $853 million, -1.2%) [source: 6]. I do not have Q2 2026 XBRL figures (the tag data available in this packet stops at Q1 2026) and the 10-Q's extracted MD&A text captured only boilerplate (Item 3/4 and Part II text on buybacks and trading plans), not a Q2 2026 Results of Operations narrative, so I cannot confirm the most recent quarter's trend directly from filing text [source: 2].

marginTrend.answer: Improving for FY2025 (GAAP operating margin +140bps to 16.1%, Adjusted Operating Margin +50bps to 15.8%, driven by 'net savings generated from our NextGen program, operational efficiencies and the beneficial impact of foreign currency exchange rate movements, partially offset by increased compensation costs and the dilutive impact of the acquisition of Belcan') [source: 4]. However, the most recent XBRL data point (Q1 2026) shows operating income essentially flat-to-down (-1.2% YoY) even as revenue grew 5.8%, which would imply modest margin compression versus Q1 2025 if it holds [source: 6]. I could not confirm whether this moderation continued into Q2 2026 because the extracted 10-Q MD&A text did not include a current-quarter Results of Operations discussion and no Q2 2026 XBRL data point was available in this packet [source: 2, 6].

guidanceChange.answer: Not determinable from available sources. The extracted 10-Q MD&A text captured only end-of-document boilerplate (Item 3 market risk, Item 4 controls, and Part II items on stock repurchases, trading plans, and exhibits), not a Business Outlook or guidance discussion for Q2/FY2026 [source: 2]. A cached news headline, 'Cognizant (CTSH) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript' (Yahoo, 2026-08-08), likely contains management guidance commentary, but only the headline was cached - the article/transcript content itself was not fetched by this pipeline, so I am not inferring guidance from it [source: 7].

catalysts.text: Aggressive, ongoing capital return: total buyback authorization of $15.5 billion (most recently expanded May 2026), with $1,153 million repurchased in Q2 2026 alone (including a $500 million accelerated share repurchase agreement) and $2,338 million still remaining as of June 30, 2026 - a real, active EPS-support mechanism.
Belcan acquisition continuing to contribute to revenue growth (260bps in FY2025) as part of Cognizant's push to build out AI-ready, industry-specific platforms and capabilities.

Improving employee retention: Voluntary Attrition - Tech Services fell to 13.9% in FY2025 from 15.9% in FY2024, alongside headcount growth to approximately 351,600 employees - a filed indicator of workforce stability supporting delivery capacity.

risks.text: The 10-Q's own qualitative goodwill impairment assessment, triggered specifically by a Q2 2026 stock price decline to 'a recent low' before partial recovery in July 2026, is a real, filed acknowledgment that the market's concern about the stock was material enough to require formal review (even though the conclusion was no impairment).

Unresolved Title VII employment discrimination class action litigation, with a certified 'bench-terminations class' and a jury trial already held on the first phase in 2023 - ongoing legal and reputational exposure as of the FY2025 10-K.

AI-driven disruption to the core IT-services labor-arbitrage business model is a live, named market narrative per cached news ('Cognizant Of AI Fears, But Also Of The Opportunity'), even though the company frames itself as an 'AI builder' benefiting from the same trend - a genuine two-sided risk/opportunity the filing itself does not fully resolve.

verdict.reasoning: The filing evidence shows genuinely improving FY2025 fundamentals (revenue +7.0%, GAAP operating margin +140bps, Adjusted EPS +11.2%) [source: 4] alongside continued Q1 2026 growth [source: 6], which does not support a clean 'value trap' read despite the stock's -21.73% six-month decline [source: 1]. But the discount is not pure sentiment noise either: the 10-Q's own goodwill-impairment qualitative assessment explicitly ties back to a real Q2 2026 stock-price decline, unresolved Title VII class-action litigation remains live, and a genuine AI-disruption narrative is circulating in current news about the company's core business model [source: 3, 5, 8]. I could not confirm whether the FY2025 margin improvement continued or reversed into Q2 2026 because the extracted MD&A text for that quarter was boilerplate rather than a results narrative, so confidence is medium rather than high.
